why_points: The pick: Rush yds lower 67.5 on Underdog. Each pick has to win 56% of the time for a typical entry to make money; the sportsbooks' fair view (fanduel 62.5, moved to this line) is 56%.
Other apps: PrizePicks 67.5. This is the best number for the lower side.
Game log, most recent first: 22, 30, 62, 8, 82, 9, 83, 68. Weighted average 40.3; went lower than 67.5 in 5 of 8 games (76% recency-weighted).
Trending down: last 3 games average 38.0 vs 50.0 in the games before.
How much he swings: game to game he typically moves about ±27.4, so the line is 1.0 of those swings above his average (standard deviations) — a meaningful gap.
Matchup: PIT has allowed -7% vs the league average to RBs (already shrunk toward average for sample size).
PFF unit matchup, for context (in the 2023-25 test it added nothing to the projection, so it is not in the numbers): -6% on his average.

PFF: PHI's run blocking vs PIT's run defense: 0.7 yds before contact per carry expected (his usual 0.9, league 1.1); he adds 3.0 after contact → -6% per carry.
Projection: we expect 42.2 rushing yards on average; in a typical game 37.0 (a few big games pull the average up, so the typical game is what we compare with the line) — 30.5 below the line.

Keeping it honest: on their own, recent games (form) say 85% and the matchup 83%. The sportsbooks are usually close to right, and these methods have only partly beaten them (weights measured on NFL week 2), so we pull them most of the way toward the market: form 62%, matchup 63%.
Bottom line: we give it 63% to win and it needs 56%. The edge is the difference: +6.9 points; that works out to about +12¢ per $1 bet over the long run.
